knowledge_gaps: Padding-ID ablation may introduce artifacts: convolution biases and normalization can produce nonzero hidden states at masked positions. Bands that include the final item also conflict with final-nonpadding readout. Define whether lag zero is excluded, retain the original readout anchor, and handle histories emptied by masking.

Receptive-field accounting must include residual branches and any normalization or pooling that mixes temporal positions. The report lacks exact lag bands, eligible-history rules, aggregation weights, uncertainty estimates, runtime limits, and a reproducible sampling procedure.

One positive and one negative support paired margins and ranking flips, not meaningful HR@10 or top-10 overlap. Those metrics require an explicitly available larger candidate set. Training-loader sensitivity also cannot establish generalization or harmful reliance on older events.

The originality rating is reasonable, but future potential remains speculative and difficulty may be understated until padding behavior and predictor consistency are verified. Zero-ID masking should be compared with controlled replacements before its effects motivate recency regularization.
